newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila departs Zaire to consult S.Africa's Mandela.
newsitem.headline: Kabila departs Zaire to consult S.Africa's Mandela.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila left Lubumbashi airport for South Africa on Wednesday to meet President Nelson Mandela, eyewitnesses said.

Kabila departed at 11.40 a.m. (0940 GMT) on a South African Air Force jet bound for Cape Town after a two-day visit to Zaire's second largest city to mark his rebels' capture of the mineral-rich Shaba province.

Kabila was due to meet Mandela for consultations on the Zaire conflict. Regional analysts said the South Africa talks would centre on arrangements for face-to-face talks between Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko.
South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo on Tuesday predicted dramatic progress within days in ending the civil war in Zaire and said Kabila could visit soon.
Kabila, speaking to Reuters ahead of his departure for Cape Town, spurned calls for a ceasefire in his drive to unseat Mobutu saying the "people are against a ceasefire".
Kabila, whose rebels now control more than half of Africa's third largest country, says he is targeting the capital Kinshasa in a bid to drive the ailing Mobutu from power.
